subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown cancel active managed exec child processes, or continue preserving yielded/backgrounded exec work unless an explicit restart or process-kill path is used?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally preserve background process work in several paths, so changing normal stop behavior can terminate operator work and needs product ownership before implementation.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel owner-approved managed active run/exec scopes through supervisor cancellation before the watchdog, with documented exceptions for preserved background work.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep normal shutdown from aborting active/background exec work and treat child-process shutdown timeouts as diagnostics, docs, or operator-runbook work rather than runtime cancellation.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this issue open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines the process-control contract, then reuse that design for shutdown semantics.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel owner-approved managed active run/exec scopes through supervisor cancellation before the watchdog, with documented exceptions for preserved background work.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the best current routing candidate from recent gateway close-handler history and the issue timeline, while the final policy likely needs shared review with process/exec owners.
